title: w0m connected-IDE policy (T192)
description: Validates project/ide-policy.json — the per-tool autoload knowledge and the non-negotiables every connected IDE's autoload surface is diffed against. ⚠️ This file exists because the policy's own `$schema` would otherwise DANGLE: `project/client-profile.json` records that w0m's and Artemio's `.w0m/sdlc.json` both point at a `./sdlc.schema.json` that does not exist, so both have passed every presence check while never being validated. Shipping a governance policy with an unresolvable $schema inside the ticket about ungoverned surfaces would be the same defect one level up.

canonical.description: The instruction surface that IS the contract; every connected IDE is measured against it.

marker.description: What proves a directory is a REAL surface rather than a name collision — content, never the directory name.

globs.description: Path-component globs that mark an openspec-generated surface. ⚠️ ONE entry, `opsx*`, verified against three repos. It briefly held `openspec*` too, on the assumption that wom7mlx's `rules/openspec.md` files were an earlier openspec layout — they are hand-written, and adding a glob because a FILENAME looked right is the very trap this policy is built around. Widen this only with evidence from the generator, never from a name.

non_negotiables.description: rule name → regex matched against every connected IDE's autoload file. An EMPTY set would make the parity gate vacuously green on every surface, so at least one is required.

skills_dir.description: Cross-checked against openspec's live registry at runtime; disagreement is a hard error, not a preference.

autoload.description: What the tool loads by itself: a path, or a LIST of paths/globs when the tool reads a rules directory (Cursor, Windsurf) or more than one surface (Gemini). `null` = unknown, which makes the tool traceable for presence but NOT parity.

autoload_shared.description: true when the autoload path is a CONVENTION several tools read (AGENTS.md). Its presence then proves nothing about which tool is connected and never raises an undeclared-surface finding.

autoload_note.description: Required: how the autoload path was established — observed, or convention-and-unverified. The distinction is the whole difference between measurement and guessing.

global_surfaces.description: AC4 — surfaces under $HOME, declared by PATH rather than derived from skillsDir, because the derivation is wrong for at least one tool (Windsurf's global rules live under ~/.codeium/).

known_not_ide_surfaces.description: Lookalikes ruled on, keyed `<unit>/<dir>`. The value is the REASON and must be non-empty — an unreasoned dismissal is how a real surface gets silenced.

delegation.description: How a surface may satisfy the contract by REFERENCE instead of restating it — the estate's actual pattern (5 of 6 sibling repos). `must_resolve` is what keeps it honest: a dangling pointer reads as compliance.

max_hops.description: How far a 'read X' chain is followed. >1 because wom7mlx delegates CLAUDE.md → AGENTS.md → the estate contract.
